_doc: Machine-readable registry of canonical parody businesses. Naming authority: world/businesses.md; depth layer: world/businesses/*.md (one card per venue). Display layer: src/sf/30a_sf_names.js + world/parody-names.json (generated). Rule: parody names only (design §11); civic/landmark kinds keep real names as scenery. All prices are GAME DOLLARS — never credits, never real USD. Supply layer: world/suppliers.json (v86 — offstage wholesale vendors + delivery runs; suppliers never enter this registry).
regulars_layer: world/regulars.json — v58: per-venue regulars (standing order, window, spot, surface knowledge, name basis, tab); spec world/regulars.md; demo world/regulars.html
storefront_layer: world/storefronts.json — v44: signage/menu-board/flyer copy per door-having venue (anchor + street tiers only); spec world/storefronts.md; demo world/storefront.html
menu_layer: world/menus.json — v72: orderable catalog per door-having venue (name, game-dollar price or 'ask', cat, when, sig, note); spec world/menus.md; demo world/menus.html
supply_layer: world/suppliers.json — v86: offstage wholesale/trade suppliers + delivery runs per door venue (the back door); spec world/suppliers.md; demo world/supply.html
permit_layer: world/permits.json — v100: per-door posted-paper walls (licenses, score cards, permits — civic agency names stay real) + door lineage (former tenants, ghost signs); spec world/permits.md; demo world/permit.html

tiers.offstage: organization with no door — employer or media surface
tiers.reserved: name claimed, not on the map

affordance_keys.event: can host a player event request (drama-manager mediated)
affordance_keys.nudge: staff here are nudge-reachable during their shifts
affordance_keys.hires: has job-board openings for player-hired characters

businesses.name: Mudhaus Coffee
hooks: morning rush 7:30-9:30 packs the counter
Marisol's closing inventory is when the tip jar gets counted twice
the blog laptop (Mission Unfiltered) appears on the manager's table after close

businesses.name: Taqueria El Farolote
hooks: post-bar rush after 1 AM is the loudest hour
Tomás prices suppliers at Valencia Growers Market on Saturdays
the notebook (Pupusería La Esperanza) lives under the counter register

businesses.name: Auerbach Hardware
businesses.corner: Mission St; flat upstairs is 9102 Mission St, Unit 2 (Victor's home)
hooks: Tuesday is repair day — tenants' work orders stack on the counter
the handshake ledger (La Esperanza loan) sits in the back drawer, off the books
construction site next door sends Cole over for hardware-store lunch talk

businesses.name: Dolores Perk
hooks: Esther and Ray hold the same two park-side tables most afternoons
sunny weekend = forty-minute line and zero seats

businesses.name: Buy-Rite Market
hooks: the whole cast's grocery runs pass through here — collision density is the content
the creamery window next door bleeds its line into the produce door

businesses.name: Buy-Rite Creamery
hooks: the line is a standing park-spillover scene — weather multiplies it

businesses.name: Il Delfino
hooks: the default date-night venue — who sits with whom is spectator information

businesses.name: Baguette About It Bakery
hooks: Hana's 4 AM bake shift is the block's first light
sellout by 13:00 most days — the closed sign is a character

businesses.name: The 600 Club
hooks: Sam pitches his rain songs here on wet Thursdays
Bex holds the back booth after tattoo shifts
open-mic nights are the event-request surface — bookings go through the bartender, in-world

businesses.name: Dandy Lion Chocolate Co.
hooks: Marcus's leisure stop — the treat he can't afford is a standing beat

businesses.name: Valencia Growers Market
hooks: Saturday mornings: Tomás walks stalls comparing tomato cases
Luz's stand regulars migrate here — she prices against them

businesses.name: Needlepointe Tattoo
hooks: walk-in Saturdays; Bex's flash sheet changes when her mood does

businesses.name: Folsom Auto & Sons
hooks: Gus talks to engines more than people; the radio is always a ballgame

businesses.name: Malik's Mini Mart
hooks: Malik knows everyone's cigarettes-and-milk order
the counter is a rumor node — whoever stops in leaves informed

businesses.name: Frutería Las Palmas
hooks: Luz's stand weather-locks to rain; her regulars notice every absence

businesses.name: Bloom & Doom Flowers
hooks: weddings and funerals both — the order book is a spoiler document

businesses.name: Golden Hour Laundromat
hooks: the 90-minute wait is the cheapest collision venue on the block — folding-table adjacency is information
Esther's Thursday-morning machines; the Friday-night laundromat date is a real genre here
the bulletin board is a second rumor node after Malik's counter

businesses.name: The Dusty Spine
hooks: June's after-school window — the YA spin rack is hers until her bus
Vera alphabetizes the free box on her day off; the clerk pretends not to notice
borrowed vs bought is a legible tell in what June carries out

businesses.name: Marooned Records
hooks: Sam's Sunday dollar-bin tithe before his park set — one 45 a week
Jules sells back the same three records every broke month; the clerk keeps a hold shelf
the in-store turntable is the counter clerk's public mood readout

businesses.name: The Musket
hooks: walk-in bar seats only — adjacency is luck the audience can watch happen
choosing this room over Il Delfino's formality is a public statement
Tomás studies the room like homework for a restaurant that doesn't exist yet

businesses.name: Flying Pannier Courier Co-op
businesses.corner: no storefront — dispatch is a locker wall
hooks: Marcus's manifest doubles as a neighborhood gossip route

businesses.name: MuleIt
hooks: always hiring because it is always losing people

businesses.name: Nimbus9
businesses.corner: remote — Nadia's kitchen table is the office
hooks: deliberately faceless; its only footprint is Nadia's laptop and her hours

businesses.name: Mission Unfiltered
businesses.corner: anonymous blog — a feed surface, not a door
hooks: posts appear after events the author couldn't have attended — a spectator puzzle
SECRET-adjacent: the blog is public, the author is not — never expose in briefings

businesses.name: Calle Justa Workers' Table
businesses.corner: no door — Thursday drop-in clinic, folding tables
hooks: rung 4 of the work grievance ladder — reads check stubs, writes demand letters the worker delivers themselves
free, bilingual; takes no cut and no unsigned complaints

businesses.name: The Rent Table
businesses.corner: no door — Wednesday table in the library community room
hooks: rung 4 of the housing grievance ladder — reads notices, checks raise math, starts paper clocks
Vera staffs the sign-in most weeks — a public volunteer fact

businesses.name: Pupusería La Esperanza
hooks: a $6,000 handshake loan from Victor is the whole capital stack — if it opens it is an earned world-event, never a spawn

businesses.name: Reserved spare names
hooks: The Watchbird (bar/lounge), Café Cometa (café) — claimed in businesses.md §2, mintable when a story needs a door. Golden Hour Laundromat minted at v30.

web._doc: v30 — business-to-business interlink layer. Economic geography as conditions: supplier runs, clientele overlap, rivalry pressure, gossip routes. Edges are facts the sim may notice (who walks where, who prices against whom), never scripts it must run. 'secret: true' edges are secret-adjacent — internal surfaces only; public clearance redacts them like secret hooks. Cast ties live in staff/hooks; the web is venue↔venue only.

kinds.supplies: one venue's stock comes from the other — a visible recurring run
kinds.spillover: one venue's crowd physically becomes the other's
kinds.rivalry: same customers, overlapping offer — pressure, never a feud
kinds.shared_clientele: same regulars by affinity — collision odds, not competition
kinds.parts_run: mid-job supply walk between working venues
kinds.gossip_route: a physical path along which neighborhood information travels
kinds.loan: money moved between venues off the books — always secret-adjacent

edges.note: the pastry case restocks off the morning bake; day-olds move at $2 — the day the case is empty is a readable anomaly
Saturday produce cases — Tomás walks stalls comparing tomato cases before the week starts
last call walks downhill into the post-1 AM burrito line — the taqueria's loudest hour is the bar's doing
when the creamery line hits the sidewalk, Perk's park-side tables take the overflow
same basket, different scale — Buy-Rite wins the peach, Malik wins at 23:00
Luz prices against the Saturday stalls; her regulars migrate weekly and she notices every defection
two date-night rooms, one neighborhood — reservation formality vs walk-in bar luck; a vibe, never a feud
the Valencia twenty-dollar loop — same browsers, different bins, one shared pastry
flash talk carries to the back booth — Bex's tattoo workload is legible in her bar occupancy
Gus walks fittings over mid-job; Victor holds them behind the counter — two old shops keeping each other honest
the folding-table bulletin board mirrors the Mini Mart's — flyers migrate between them within days
Marcus's manifest includes the Delfino pickup — the courier sees the date-night room before anyone talks about it
Ida and Luz trade stem scraps for fruit — the corner smells like both by noon
the $6,000 handshake — Victor's back-drawer ledger funds a restaurant that does not exist

corridor_flips_note: The second-wave parody names (v16 — e.g. Tacobulous, Hole in Fun, Centro Cultural La Misión) live in SF_PARODY_NAMES / parody-names.json, not here: they are signage-level venues with no cast ties. Promote one to a card only when a routine, job, or storyline attaches to it. Promoted at v30: The Dusty Spine (Dog Eared Books), Marooned Records (Stranded Records), The Musket (Beretta) — plus Golden Hour Laundromat minted from the reserved list.
